brand.name: MeshMesh
brand.tagline: Build production-grade Salesforce work with AI agents.
brand.voice: Clean, scannable, confident-but-not-hyped. Product-update tone (Stripe/Linear/Vercel). Lead with outcomes and numbers. Avoid: game-changing, revolutionary, supercharge, seamlessly, leverage, utilize.
sources: MeshMesh Studio app design system (packages/frontend/styles/globals.css, apps/desktop)
MeshMesh Salesforce Pilot Impact Report (Feb 8 – Mar 29, 2026)

colors.description: Master palette. MeshMesh is dark-first for flagship/editorial output (reports, decks); light surfaces are provided for email and web where a light canvas is expected. Coral is the brand signature (carried over exactly from the app primary); mint signals positive outcomes/metrics; amber/copper is the warm editorial accent from the report artwork.

fontFamily.sans: 'Geist Sans', 'Geist', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

webfont.note: The MeshMesh app loads Geist via Adobe Typekit (use.typekit.net/slz7jmg.css). Geist is also on Google Fonts; either works. System stack is the fallback.

desktop.note: For desktop artifacts (decks, print) install the font as 'Geist' / 'Geist Mono' — NOT the Typekit name 'Geist Sans'. Static OFL TTFs are vendored in assets/fonts/ (Geist-Regular, Geist-Bold, GeistMono-Regular, GeistMono-Medium). The PPTX deck embeds these so it renders on-brand without a local install.

typography.conventions: Headings are light/regular weight with tight tracking. Section eyebrows are small uppercase with wide (~0.18em) tracking in muted or coral. Numerals/metrics may use the primary (coral) or positive (mint) accent.

shadows.philosophy: Minimal/flat. Prefer 1px borders over shadows on dark surfaces.

primaryLockup.description: Official co-branded horizontal lockup: mesh mark + 'MeshMesh' wordmark + 'from [cloud] Salesforce' endorsement. Use this wherever a horizontal logo fits (nav, email header, hero, footer). viewBox 0 0 802 230.

email.note: Email clients (Gmail, Outlook) do not render SVG. Use the PNG for any email and host it at a public https URL.

logo.mark: Single-path evenodd mesh / triangular-lattice glyph. One color; recolors cleanly. Use the mark alone only for square/compact contexts (favicon, avatar, app icon, tight badges) where the full lockup will not fit.
logo.usage: Prefer the primary co-branded lockup. White lockup on dark backgrounds (default, dark-first), black lockup on light. Use the mark alone only when a horizontal lockup will not fit. The 'from Salesforce' endorsement (cloud #00B3FF, navy #001E5B) is part of the lockup art — do not recolor or separate it. Keep clear space of at least the mark height ÷ 2 on all sides. Never stretch, rotate, or recolor outside the approved variants.
logo.hosting: Replace the relative paths with public HTTPS URLs when a template is used outside this folder (email clients require absolute URLs).

coverArt.description: Official MeshMesh cover / banner art — abstract liquid-glass forms on retro-wave stripes. Used for collection covers, recipe covers, and hero banners. 3:2 landscape. Left side is a text-safe negative-space zone; overlay titles there with a dark left-to-right scrim so white type stays legible on every colorway (see templates/cover-template.html).
coverArt.textSafeZone: left ~40% — apply linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(10,10,10,0.74), rgba(10,10,10,0.40) 40%, transparent 66%) as a scrim under the text

colorways.name: teal
colorways.theme: data / positive — Data Cloud, metrics, growth

coverArt.concepts: assets/covers-ideas/ holds 10 generated vector cover concepts (not the official art).

landingPage.description: Conventions for a one-page marketing/landing site in the kit, as built in examples/meshmesh-landing.html. Dark-first, cover-art hero, single accent restraint. Self-contained: for offline/Quick-Look-safe delivery, inline all assets (logo lockup + cover art) as base64 data URIs so the file has no external subresources.

hero.background: Full-bleed cover art (blue colorway, 'MeshMesh Cover 2') pinned right center / cover, over the #0A0A0A canvas.
hero.scrim: Two stacked scrims keep left-aligned white type legible over the art: horizontal linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(10,10,10,0.96) 0%, 0.90 42%, 0.62 66%, 0.12 100%) plus a bottom vertical fade linear-gradient(0deg, #0A0A0A 0%, rgba(10,10,10,0.35) 14%, transparent 34%).
hero.headline: Headline is solid white — do NOT color or highlight individual words. A mono kicker (// …) sits above it; the numbered section eyebrow was dropped.

metrics.note: On the landing page, hero stats and ROI figures are WHITE (var(--mm-fg)), not mint/coral — the cover art and coral CTAs already carry the color, so white numerals read cleaner. Units (e.g. 'hrs') and labels stay muted/subtle. This is a landing-page choice; long-form reports still follow the master convention (coral or mint numerals).

integrationMarquee.description: Product/integration logos scroll horizontally in a single row rather than wrapping/stacking — avoids the row getting chopped off on narrow viewports.
integrationMarquee.technique: Two identical .marquee-track flex rows (second aria-hidden) inside an overflow:hidden .marquee, animated transform:translateX(0 → -100%) at ~40s linear infinite for a seamless loop. Edge fade via mask-image linear-gradient. Pause on hover. prefers-reduced-motion: reduce → drop the animation and fall back to overflow-x:auto.

videoEmbed.rationale: Prefer a YouTube iframe over an inline <video> with a remote src. In the macOS Quick Look sandbox a remote <video> src degrades the whole document's styling (author links/buttons render unstyled); a YouTube iframe does not. YouTube error 153 only appears when viewing over file:// (null origin) — serve over http (e.g. python3 -m http.server) and it plays.

footer.description: Footer leads with the white co-branded lockup + one-line tagline on the left and a compact two-column link nav on the right, above a mono compliance/copyright row.
footer.gotcha: Scope the sticky-header styles to the header only. A global `nav {position:sticky; top:0}` rule will also catch a footer <nav> and stick it to the top of the viewport — use a <div> (e.g. .foot-nav) for the footer link group, not <nav>.

messaging.description: Foundational brand messaging & copy governance. LLM-ready: rules are binary/deterministic, every pillar ships Do/Don't examples, and the whole system is mirrored in a machine-readable schema. Full docs in messaging/. Derived from 'Meet MeshMesh' (v.07242026) and 'MeshMesh Product & Technology Overview' (Jul 2026).
messaging.positioningStatement: For Salesforce Solution Engineers, Technical Architects, Admins, Trailblazers, Partners, FDEs, Professional Services, Customer Success, and Account teams, MeshMesh is the Headless 360 orchestration platform that plans and executes end-to-end Salesforce work from plain-language intent, because it pairs deep validated knowledge of 40+ Salesforce products with a three-context intelligence model that compounds with every run and stops only when outcomes are verified.
messaging.coreMessage: MeshMesh collapses Salesforce setup from months to minutes. You define the outcome, approve the plan, and MeshMesh executes it end-to-end — and gets better with every run.

maestro.vision: We make the complex, Salesforce simple.
maestro.definition: Salesforce's new AI-native, agent-driven initiative to make using and implementing any Salesforce product simple.
maestro.meshmeshRole: MeshMesh is part of Maestro — the engine proving it works, today.
maestro.approvedLine: Maestro is the vision. MeshMesh is the engine proving it works, today.
maestro.note: Lead with Maestro at the strategy/executive level, MeshMesh at the product level. Keep the Maestro value motion (Diagnose → Fix → Innovate) distinct from the MeshMesh task flow (Define → Approve → Execute).

pillars: Autonomous end-to-end execution (it finishes the job)
Built for business users, in plain language
Compounding intelligence (gets better with every run)
voiceRules: Address the reader in second person.
Lead with an outcome or a number, not an adjective.
Active voice in headlines and CTAs.
One value claim per sentence; no stacked superlatives.
Keep sentences short — aim for ~10 words (principle, not a hard gate); one idea per sentence.
Zero words from the forbidden list.
Concrete verbs (plan, build, configure, deploy, test, document).
Pair any 'autonomous' claim with the human approval gate.
Every statistic in long-form carries its source/qualifier.
Keep it sparse — cut every removable word. Less is more.
Plain English at a high-school reading level; no corporate jargon or flowery words.
Sound human, not generated — no LLM-tell phrases (delve, unlock, empower, elevate, 'in today's fast-paced world', etc.).

lexiconHighlights.MeshMesh: one word, both M's capital — never 'Mesh Mesh' or 'Meshmesh'
lexiconHighlights.Salesforce: always 'Salesforce' in external copy — never 'SFDC' or 'salesforce.com'
lexiconHighlights.sandbox: 'Salesforce sandbox' and 'sandbox syncing' are correct; do NOT call MeshMesh's own runtime a 'sandbox' (use 'secure, isolated environment')
lexiconHighlights.Agentforce: a partner concept, not a rival — 'MeshMesh doesn't replace Agentforce, it builds Agentforce… and beyond'
